title: Bonus Episode: The Most Boring Podcast Ever (Or, What to Do With Yourself During COVID-19) with Erin Westgate, PhD

sentences.en: The first confirmed case of COVID-19 in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国首例确诊的新冠肺炎病例

sentences.en: was identified in January.
sentences.zh: 于一月份被发现。

sentences.en: By March, most of us had been strongly advised, if not ordered, to keep at least six feet away from other people in public and pretty much to confine ourselves to our homes.
sentences.zh: 到了三月份，我们大多数人都被强烈建议——如果不是强制要求的话——在公共场所与他人保持至少六英尺的距离，并且基本上要呆在家裡。

sentences.en: As a result, many of us are unable to visit friends or family.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们许多人无法探望朋友或家人。

sentences.en: We can't go out to a movie, to the gym, or out to dinner.
sentences.zh: 我们不能去看电影、去健身房或外出用餐。

sentences.en: In short, the coronavirus has radically curtailed the way many of us live.
sentences.zh: 简而言之，冠状病毒彻底改变了我们许多人的生活方式。

sentences.en: So are we bored yet?
sentences.zh: 那我们现在觉得无聊了吗？

sentences.en: And if we are bored, is that a problem?
sentences.zh: 如果我们觉得无聊，这算是一个问题吗？

sentences.en: Is boredom bad?
sentences.zh: 无聊是一件坏事吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that explores the links between psychology and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》（Speaking of Psychology），这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。

sentences.en: What does psychology tell us about boredom?
sentences.zh: 心理学告诉我们关于无聊的什么？

sentences.en: And why should we care?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要关注它？

sentences.en: Is boredom even a legitimate area for psychologists to study?
sentences.zh: 无聊甚至是心理学家研究的一个合法的领域吗？

sentences.en: What can we do during these strange times to keep from being bored or to use our boredom productively?
sentences.zh: 在这段奇特的时期，我们可以做些什么来避免感到无聊，或者如何富有成效地利用我们的无聊？

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Erin Westgate, an assistant professor of psychology at the University of Florida, where she studies boredom, interest,
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是佛罗里达大学心理学助理教授埃林·韦斯特盖特（Erin Westgate）博士，她在那里研究无聊、兴趣，

sentences.en: and why some thoughts are more engaging than others.
sentences.zh: 以及为什么有些想法比其他想法更能吸引人。

sentences.en: Much of her research has been on the conditions under which people enjoy or do not enjoy their own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 她的许多研究都集中在人们享受或不享受自己想法的条件上。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology,
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学话你知》，

sentences.en: Dr. Westgate.
sentences.zh: 韦斯特盖特博士。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Let me start by throwing you a big softball.
sentences.zh: 让我先向你抛出一个非常简单的问题来热热身。

sentences.en: So what is boredom, and how is it different from other states of mental inactivity?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是无聊，它与其他的精神不活跃状态有何不同？

sentences.en: So boredom is actually an emotion.
sentences.zh: 所以，无聊其实是一种情绪。

sentences.en: There's often a lot of confusion about this.
sentences.zh: 对此经常有很多困惑。

sentences.en: Like, is boredom actually a feeling I have?
sentences.zh: 比如，无聊真的是我的一种感觉吗？

sentences.en: Is it an emotion?
sentences.zh: 它是一种情绪吗？

sentences.en: Is it a state where I'm not feeling anything at all?
sentences.zh: 它是我完全没有任何感觉的状态吗？

sentences.en: We actually, there's been a lot of debate in psychology about this, but the growing consensus is that boredom is an emotion like any other that you experience,
sentences.zh: 实际上，心理学对此有很多争论，但日益形成的共识是，无聊就像你体验到的任何其他情绪一样，

sentences.en: like anger or sadness, and that we define it as those cases where you're not able to engage
sentences.zh: 比如愤怒或悲伤，我们将其定义为这样一种情况：你无法有意义地投入到

sentences.en: meaningfully in whatever it is that you're doing, either because you're not able to pay attention or because whatever it is that you're doing just doesn't feel meaningful to you.
sentences.zh: 你正在做的任何事情中，要么是因为你无法集中注意力，要么是因为你所做的事情对你来说根本没有意义。

sentences.en: Well, as I mentioned a moment ago, a lot of us are stuck in our homes with very little to distract us.
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才提到的，我们很多人都被困在家裡，几乎没有什么东西可以分散注意力。

sentences.en: Are you hearing that boredom is on the rise as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic?
sentences.zh: 你是否听到由于COVID-19大流行而导致无聊情绪正在上升？

sentences.en: There's some interesting research out of Italy, actually, that looked at folks in quarantine
sentences.zh: 事实上，来自意大利的一些有趣研究调查了隔离中的人们，

sentences.en: right now that suggests that they themselves said that the second biggest sort of downside to being stuck at home was lack of freedom first, obviously.
sentences.zh: 目前这表明他们自己表示，被困在家里带来的第二大负面影响是缺乏自由——显而易见，第一是自由。

sentences.en: But the second most problematic thing that they were experiencing was boredom, even more than the social isolation and feelings of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 但他们经历的第二大问题是无聊，甚至超过了社交隔离和孤独感。

sentences.en: So I think it really depends a lot.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这很大程度上取决于具体情况。

sentences.en: I think certainly there are some people who may be home homeschooling kids and trying to work from home and who are not bored that if anything, they may be feeling
sentences.zh: 我认为当然有些人可能在家裡辅导孩子并试图在家工作，他们並不觉得无聊，如果有的话，他们可能会感到

sentences.en: overwhelmed and anxious.
sentences.zh: 压抑和焦虑。

sentences.en: But I think there's an awful lot of us who are at home and suddenly find ourselves without the routines that structured our lives or the tasks that we've spent most of our
sentences.zh: 但我认为有相当多的人呆在家裡，突然发现自己没有了规范我们生活的日常，也没有了我们花大部分时间去做的任务，

sentences.en: days doing and stuck with those long sort of periods of time with nothing to do and limits on what you can do about it.
sentences.zh: 只能面对那些漫长的时间段，无所事事，且对这种状况无能为力。

sentences.en: I think a lot of us are feeling a bit bored.
sentences.zh: 我想我们很多人都觉得有点无聊。

sentences.en: What made you want to study boredom?
sentences.zh: 是什么让你想要研究无聊？

sentences.en: I mean, were you sort of in a state of boredom and it hit you that, wow, this is something I need to think about?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你当时是处于一种无聊的状态，然后突然意识到，哇，这是我需要思考的事情吗？

sentences.en: You know, it's always, I always get a laugh when I tell people I study boredom.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每当我告诉别人我研究无聊时，我总是能引来笑声。

sentences.en: People are like, oh, like, did you always grow up wanting to like be a boredom researcher?
sentences.zh: 人们会问，哦，比如，你从小就一直想成为一名无聊研究员吗？

sentences.en: No, absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 不，绝对不是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't think that's anything little kids.
sentences.zh: 我认为任何小孩子都不会这样。

sentences.en: Haven't heard that one from a kid yet.
sentences.zh: 还没从孩子那里听到过这种说法。

sentences.en: No, right?
sentences.zh: 不，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, oh, I really want to study boredom one day.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我有一天真的想研究无聊。

sentences.en: I sort of fell into studying boredom because I was doing earlier work on whether people enjoy being alone with their own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 我之所以涉足无聊研究，是因为我之前做过关于人们是否喜欢独自呆在自己思绪中的研究。

sentences.en: So we all find ourselves stuck at times such as at the stoplight or just, you know, waiting in line when
sentences.zh: 所以我们都会发现在某些时候被困住，比如在红绿灯前，或者只是，你知道，排队等待的时候，

sentences.en: it would be nice if we could sort of sit back mentally and daydream or just sort of enjoy our own thoughts.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能在精神上坐下来做白日梦，或者只是享受自己的思绪，那该多好。

sentences.en: And when I started graduate school, I was interested in this question.
sentences.zh: 当我开始读研究生时，我对这个问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: I started doing research on this question and found that a lot of us really struggle to do this.
sentences.zh: 我开始对这个问题进行研究，发现我们很多人在这个方面真的很挣扎。

sentences.en: It's not as easy to simply sit back and intentionally have a pleasant daydream as you might think.
sentences.zh: 像你想象的那样，简单地坐下来有意地进行一个愉快的白日梦并不是那么容易的。

sentences.en: And in one study, for instance, we even found that when you ask people to do this on demand in the laboratory, we tell them, you know, sit down, try to think for pleasure.
sentences.zh: 例如，在一项研究中，我们甚至发现，当你要求人们在实验室里按要求这样做时，我们告诉他们，你知道，坐下来，试着为了快乐而思考。

sentences.en: Um, but if you want, you can, you can shock yourself with this little electric shock here, about 67% of the men and 25% of the women chose to shock
sentences.zh: 嗯，但如果你愿意，你可以用这个小电击器电击自己，大约67%的男性和25%的女性选择电击

sentences.en: themselves rather than just sit and think.
sentences.zh: 自己，而不是只坐着思考。

sentences.en: And when we asked them why, uh, they kind of looked at us like, well done.
sentences.zh: 当我们问他们为什么时，嗯，他们看着我们的表情就像是在说，干得漂亮。

sentences.en: They were like, well, it was really boring.
sentences.zh: 他们说，嗯，真的很无聊。

sentences.en: Cause that's such not an answer, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为这根本不算是一个答案，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I was bored.
sentences.zh: 我很无聊。

sentences.en: So I shocked myself and I was so intrigued by that question.
sentences.zh: 所以我电击了自己，我对此问题深感兴趣。

sentences.en: Um, and I sort of pivoted a little from like, why do people, do people enjoy daydreaming?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我稍微转变了一下方向，从“人们为什么、人们喜欢白日梦吗？”

sentences.en: Why is it so hard to daydream to like, what is this strange state that makes people willing to shock themselves?
sentences.zh: “为什么白日梦这么难？”转向“这是什么奇怪的状态，让人宁愿电击自己？”

sentences.en: Why are they bored?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们会觉得无聊？

sentences.en: Uh, can we figure out how to make people not bored?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们能找出如何让人们不觉得无聊的方法吗？

sentences.en: And can we understand what people do when they are bored?
sentences.zh: 我们能了解人们在无聊时会做什么吗？

sentences.en: So I really, I really had a sort of a shift that came out of the research I was doing and what the participants themselves were telling us.
sentences.zh: 所以我的确，我的这种转变源于我当时正在做的研究以及参与者自己告诉我们的信息。

sentences.en: And I realized, uh, I like to say boredom is actually pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，嗯，我喜欢说无聊其实挺有趣的。

sentences.en: And that's not something I would have, uh, I would have said 10 years ago before I started doing this work.
sentences.zh: 这不是我，嗯，在十年前开始这项工作之前会说的话。

sentences.en: So that's an interesting study that you, that you did.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项你做过的很有趣的研究。

sentences.en: And I know that, um, you found differences between men and women.
sentences.zh: 我知道，嗯，你发现在男性和女性之间存在差异。

sentences.en: And I'm also wondering, I mean, you can talk about that in a moment, but did people shock themselves more than once?
sentences.zh: 我也想知道，我的意思是，你等一下可以谈谈这个，人们电击自己不止一次吗？

sentences.en: I mean, was it just out of curiosity or would they just sit there and do it a couple of times because what the heck?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这只是出于好奇，还是他们只是坐在那里做好几次，因为管他呢？

sentences.en: You know, it's, it's the darndest thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真是，太不可思议了。

sentences.en: They did it multiple times.
sentences.zh: 他们做了好几次。

sentences.en: Um, I know, I know we were like, the results came in and we were like, well, let's give people the benefit of the doubt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我知道，我知道当时结果出来了，我们在想，好吧，我们还是对人抱有善意吧。

sentences.en: Maybe they, you know, just wanted to see if we, maybe they wanted to call our bluff.
sentences.zh: 也许他们，你知道，只是想看看我们，也许他们想挑战我们的虚张声势。

sentences.en: Maybe they weren't sure if we were really serious about it, or maybe, um, they just wanted to see what would happen.
sentences.zh: 也许他们不确定我们是不是真的认真的，或者也许，嗯，他们只是想看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Uh, but the majority of people that shocked themselves, shocked themselves more than once.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是那些电击自己的人中，大多数都电击了不止一次。

sentences.en: And we had one person who, um, we actually excluded from the data because he shocked himself like over, I forget now it's over like 75 times.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个人，嗯，我们实际上把他排除在数据之外了，因为他电击了自己差不多，我忘了现在是多少，超过75次。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And it was only, he was having a good time, huh?
sentences.zh: 而且仅仅是，他当时玩得很开心，对吧？

sentences.en: Or something.
sentences.zh: 或者别的什么。

sentences.en: Um, it was only a 20 minute period or a 15 minute period.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那其实只是一个20分钟或15分钟的时间段。

sentences.en: So we actually had a research assistant go back and see if our machine was even capable of shocking someone that many times, like maybe like the machine was broken.
sentences.zh: 所以我们实际上让一个研究助理回去查看我们的机器是否真的能够电击一个人那么多下，比如机器是不是坏了。

sentences.en: So this wonderful, uh, undergraduate research assistant
sentences.zh: 所以这个出色的，嗯，本科研究助理

sentences.en: for science sat there and shocked herself like a hundred times just to see if the machine would work.
sentences.zh: 为了科学坐在那里电击了自己大约一百次，只是为了看看机器是否工作。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So yeah, we don't think it was something like just calling our bluff or, um, and the other
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们认为这不仅仅是挑战我们的虚张声势，或者，嗯，还有另一件事，

sentences.en: thing is that all these people, we gave them a taste of the shock upfront and we had them experience it and rate it.
sentences.zh: 我们预先让这些人体验了一下电击的滋味，让他们感受并对其进行评价。

sentences.en: They could tell us whether they enjoyed it or didn't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以告诉我们他们是喜欢还是不喜欢。

sentences.en: And you know, everyone basically says they don't enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，基本上每个人都说他们不喜欢。

sentences.en: And we said, okay, like, imagine we give you $5.
sentences.zh: 然后我们说，好吧，想象我们给你5美元。

sentences.en: How much would you pay to not be shocked again?
sentences.zh: 为了不再挨电击，你愿意付多少钱？

sentences.en: And most of these people that went on to shock themselves, uh, said they'd pay on average about $2 to not be shocked.
sentences.zh: 而大多数继续电击自己的人，嗯，说他们平均愿意支付大约2美元来避免电击。

sentences.en: And that's, yeah, I know.
sentences.zh: 就是这样，是的，我知道。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: It's like, we're strangers to ourselves.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，我们对彼此而言都是陌生人。

sentences.en: It's a failure of imagination.
sentences.zh: 这是想象力的失败。

sentences.en: Um, I think we don't know how we're going to feel in the future.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我们不知道自己未来会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: I think we don't realize how boring something might be and how motivated we can feel when we are bored to do something, um, even to do anything to stop feeling that way.
sentences.zh: 我想我们没有意识到某事可能会有多无聊，以及当我们在无聊时，为了做点什么、为了停止那种感觉，我们可以有多强的动力。

sentences.en: So that raises a question for me, which is whether there's anything useful about boredom or is it detrimental or is it somehow both?
sentences.zh: 这就引发了我的一个问题，那就是无聊到底有没有用处，还是有害的，或者某种程度上两者皆有？

sentences.en: Uh, D all of the above.
sentences.zh: 嗯，以上皆是。

sentences.en: Boredom is useful when it's working correctly.
sentences.zh: 当无聊正常运作时，它是很有用的。

sentences.en: So I always like to say that boredom is like pain.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是喜欢说无聊就像疼痛。

sentences.en: Uh, no one wants to experience pain.
sentences.zh: 没有人想经历疼痛。

sentences.en: Pain is unpleasant.
sentences.zh: 疼痛是不愉快的。

sentences.en: It hurts, but it's also really, really useful because it tells us that there's something wrong going on in our bodies.
sentences.zh: 它很痛，但它也非常非常有用，因为它告诉我们我们的身体出了问题。

sentences.en: And it's a way of alerting us to that problem and motivating us to take steps to stop it.
sentences.zh: 这是提醒我们注意该问题并促使我们采取步骤来阻止它的一种方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And boredom and other negative emotions as well, act in the same way.
sentences.zh: 无聊和其他负面情绪也是如此，它们的作用是一样的。

sentences.en: Boredom tells us, Hey, look, something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 无聊告诉我们，嘿，看，出问题了。

sentences.en: Um, in this case that we either can't pay attention to what we're doing cause it's too hard or too easy, but because what we're doing doesn't feel
sentences.zh: 嗯，在这种情况下，我们要么无法集中注意力做我们正在做的事，因为它太难或太容易，而是因为我们在做的事情感覺

sentences.en: meaningful to us, but whatever it is, boredom says, stop, this is hurting us mentally.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说没有意义，但无论如何，无聊都在说：停下，这对我们的精神有害。

sentences.en: Um, can you do something about it?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你能为此做点什么吗？

sentences.en: And so boredom is really important because it signals instances to us when we're not meaningfully engaged in the world and it gives us an opportunity to fix it.
sentences.zh: 因此，无聊非常重要，因为它向我们发出信号，表明我们没有积极地参与到世界中，并给我们提供了解决这个问题的机会。

sentences.en: Um, that said, that's only healthy and adaptive in cases where you can do something about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，话虽如此，这只有在你能对它采取行动的情况下才是健康和适应性的。

sentences.en: If you're trapped, for instance, in, um, in a room by psychologists with nothing else to do, but shock yourself, there's not really any good solution available to you.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你被心理学家困在，嗯，一个房间里，无事可做只能电击自己，那么你其实并没有什么好的解决方案。

sentences.en: So in that case, boredom is an adaptive signal, but it can come a problem when we don't have good options on the table to fix it.
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，无聊是一种适应性信号，但当我们没有好的选项来解决它时，它就会成为一个问题。

sentences.en: If you're stuck in the room and you have nothing figuratively to do to stop feeling bored other than to shock yourself, uh, then people will shock themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果你被困在房间里，除了电击自己之外，形而上学地说没有什么可做来停止感到无聊，嗯，那么人们就会电击自己。

sentences.en: And that obviously is not good.
sentences.zh: 这显然是不好的。

sentences.en: So I, I, I do like the analogy that boredom is like pain.
sentences.zh: 所以我，我，我确实喜欢这个类比：无聊就像疼痛。

sentences.en: It's healthy and useful and important information, but it can become chronic.
sentences.zh: 它是健康、有用且重要的信息，但它可能会变成慢性的。

sentences.en: And when it becomes chronic, it doesn't serve as that useful signal anymore.
sentences.zh: 当它变成慢性时，它就不再起到那种有用的信号作用了。

sentences.en: And we can vary in the ways we respond to it.
sentences.zh: 我们对它的反应方式可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: We really want to treat the underlying cause of that pain or that boredom.
sentences.zh: 我们真的想要治疗这种疼痛或无聊的根本原因。

sentences.en: We don't want to just treat the bad feelings and make them go away without fixing those underlying issues.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望只治疗不好的感觉并让它们消失，而不去解决那些根本问题。

sentences.en: That sounds almost like boredom can morph into depression.
sentences.zh: 这听起来几乎就像无聊可以演变成抑郁症。

sentences.en: Is, is that what happens to us?
sentences.zh: 是，这就是发生在我们身上的事吗？

sentences.en: It's not clear.
sentences.zh: 目前还不清楚。

sentences.en: Um, there's a lot of discussion and debate right now on what exactly the relationship is between boredom and depression.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在有很多关于无聊和抑郁之间确切关系的讨论和辩论。

sentences.en: Boredom is certainly a feature of depression in many cases.
sentences.zh: 在许多情况下，无聊当然是抑郁症的一个特征。

sentences.en: Um, people who are depressed often talk about a lack of motivation, uh, an inability to find anything meaningful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，抑郁的人经常谈论缺乏动力，嗯，无法找到任何有意义的事情。

sentences.en: They struggle to pay attention.
sentences.zh: 他们很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: These are all things we see in boredom and many depressed people report feeling bored a lot.
sentences.zh: 这些都是我们在无聊中看到的现象，许多抑郁的人都报告说经常感到无聊。

sentences.en: What's not clear is if depression causes boredom, um, or if boredom causes depression or what I think may be most likely is that situations that cause chronic boredom.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚的是，究竟是抑郁导致了无聊，嗯，还是无聊导致了抑郁，或者我认为最有可能的情况是，导致慢性无聊的情況。

sentences.en: So being in situations where you're sort of stuck, where you don't have any good options on the table, that's going to make you bored.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，处于那种你被困住、没有好选择的处境中，这会让你感到无聊。

sentences.en: That's also over time going to make you depressed independent of whether you're bored or not.
sentences.zh: 随时间推移，无论你是否无聊，这也都会让你感到抑郁。

sentences.en: So I think it's very complicated and that's one of the, you know, there's a few questions that I think that are really at the forefront of boredom research right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这非常复杂，这也是其中一个，你知道的，我认为现在处于无聊研究最前沿的几个问题之一。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of them is untangling how boredom and depression and a lot of really maladaptive behaviors associated with both
sentences.zh: 我认为其中之一就是厘清无聊、抑郁以及与其相关的大量真正适应不良的行为

sentences.en: them, uh, like substance use and alcohol use, how they're all interrelated and who's causing who.
sentences.zh: 比如物质使用和酒精使用，它们之间是如何相互关联的，以及谁是导致谁的原因。

sentences.en: Oh, good questions.
sentences.zh: 哦，好问题。

sentences.en: So are you using, um, brain scans, fMRIs, things like that to determine when people say they're bored or can, can you tell based on what their brains look like, whether they're
sentences.zh: 那么，你们是否正在使用，嗯，脑部扫描、功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）诸如此类的方法来确定人们说他们无聊的时候，或者你们能不能根据他们大脑的样子，判断出他們是否

sentences.en: experiencing something other than boredom?
sentences.zh: 正在经历除无聊之外的事情？

sentences.en: So we usually in studies of boredom and all emotion really rely pretty face validly on what people tell us.
sentences.zh: 所以在关于无聊以及所有情绪的研究中，我们通常相当直观地依赖于人们告诉我们的内容。

sentences.en: Uh, there's been a lot of debate in psychology about how do you best measure something like happiness or you measure best measure something like boredom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在心理学中，关于如何最好地衡量幸福感或无聊感，一直有很多争论。

sentences.en: And the consensus is largely that the best, most reliable way is to simply ask people what they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 而大家的共识基本上是，最好、最可靠的方法就是直接问人们他们的感受。

sentences.en: Now people can't tell you why they're feeling that way.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们无法告诉你他们为什么会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: Um, if they try, if you ask them, why are you bored?
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果他们试图去解释，如果你问他们，你为什么会觉得无聊？

sentences.en: Uh, they may have theories for it.
sentences.zh: 呃，他们可能会给出一些理论。

sentences.en: They may have causal ideas for it and they may think that's why they're bored, but we know that people can't actually
sentences.zh: 他们可能会有一些因果方面的想法，并且他们可能认为这就是他们觉得无聊的原因，但我们知道人们其实并不能

sentences.en: accurately introspect on those things.
sentences.zh: 对这些事情进行准确的内省。

sentences.en: They can't actually tell us why they're bored because we don't have access to that information mentally, but they can tell us what they're feeling.
sentences.zh: 他们其实无法告诉我们他们为什么会觉得无聊，因为我们在心理上无法获取那些信息，但他们可以告诉我们他们的感受。

sentences.en: Uh, there is some work looking at boredom, uh, in terms of sort of neuroscience.
sentences.zh: 呃，有一些关于无聊的研究，从某种神经科学的角度来看。

sentences.en: There's not a lot of it.
sentences.zh: 这类研究并不多。

sentences.en: Most of it's been done by James Denkert and his crew, uh, out of Canada.
sentences.zh: 其中大部分是由来自加拿大的詹姆斯·登克特（James Denkert）和他的团队完成的。

sentences.en: Um, I haven't gone that much that direction, partly because of the work by Kristen Lindquist and Lisa Feldman Barrett and
sentences.zh: 嗯，我没有往那个方向深入太多，部分原因是克里斯滕·林德奎斯特（Kristen Lindquist）、莉莎·费尔德曼·巴雷特（Lisa Feldman Barrett）以及

sentences.en: others that suggest that there aren't really good neural markers of specific emotions in the brain
sentences.zh: 其他人的研究表明，在大脑中其实并没有针对特定情绪的良好神经标记物，

sentences.en: that when you look at anger and sadness and fear, people's brains all kind of look pretty similar that you can't really reliably distinguish one emotion from each other.
sentences.zh: 当你观察愤怒、悲伤和恐惧时，人们的大脑看起来其实都挺相似的，你无法真正可靠地将一种情绪与另一种情绪区分开来。

sentences.en: So I think there's lots of important neuroscience to be done in boredom, but it's not a direction that I've really pursued.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，在无聊感的研究中还有很多重要的神经科学工作要做，但这并不是我真正追求的方向。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: So the neurons just fire no matter what you're feeling something intense and that's what they see.
sentences.zh: 所以，不管你感受到的是什么强烈的情绪，神经元都会放电，而这正是他们所看到的。

sentences.en: Uh, we're still working on that question, but we, we do think that what seems to be happening is that there's an affective response.
sentences.zh: 呃，我们还在研究这个问题，但我们确实认为，似乎正在发生的是存在一种情感反应。

sentences.en: When we say affect, meaning like emotion, that when people are feeling lots of big emotions, you do see lots of activation in the brain,
sentences.zh: 当我们说“情感”（affect）时，指的是像情绪一样的东西，当人们感受到许多强烈的情绪时，你确实会看到大脑中有大量活动，

sentences.en: but it's hard to tell just from looking at the brain, whether that's an anger response or a fear response or what exactly is going on in those cases.
sentences.zh: 但仅凭观察大脑很难判断这究竟是愤怒反应、恐惧反应，还是在这些情况下到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Back in the days when I used to be able to go outside and see people, I would notice a lot of folks had their phones in their hands all the time.
sentences.zh: 在过去我还能出门去看人们的日子里，我会注意到很多人手里总是拿着手机。

sentences.en: We're using smartphones, tablets, computers constantly.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在使用智能手机、平板电脑和电脑。

sentences.en: Is that having an impact on our ability to experience boredom?
sentences.zh: 这是否正在对我们体验无聊的能力产生影响？

sentences.en: Are we keeping ourselves away from the normal experience of boredom by substituting these screens?
sentences.zh: 我们是否通过用这些屏幕替代来让自己远离了无聊的正常体验？

sentences.en: You know, that's a question that I always get.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是我经常被问到的一个问题。

sentences.en: And the quick answer is we don't know.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是：我们不知道。

sentences.en: Um, certainly if you look throughout history, like every generation has had its version of the smartphone.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当然，如果你回顾历史，就像每一代人都有其版本的智能手机一样。

sentences.en: Um, if you like look back far enough, you start seeing people complain about newspapers, how people are
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你回溯得足够远，你就会开始看到人们抱怨报纸，抱怨人们

sentences.en: just, you know, reading on the subway instead of, you know, novels were the big vice back in the day
sentences.zh: 只是，你知道的，在地铁里阅读而不是……你知道的，小说在当年可是个大恶习，

sentences.en: when they first came out, like, Oh, people are like ignoring the world for these fake melodramas that aren't even real.
sentences.zh: 当它们刚出现时，人们就会说：“哦，大家为了这些甚至都不是真的虚假情节剧而忽略了现实世界。”

sentences.en: So I, you know, I really wish I had a time machine as a social psychologiSt. I like, you know, people always ask, like, if you had a superpower, what would you do?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，作为一名社会心理学家，我真的很希望自己能有一台时光机。我喜欢，你知道的，人们总是问，如果你有一种超能力，你会做什么？

sentences.en: I would time travel and I would take my questionnaires and my studies and I'd go back in time and, and see.
sentences.zh: 我会进行时间旅行，带上我的问卷和研究，回到过去，然后去看看。

sentences.en: Um, what we do know is when we look at, this isn't exactly boredom, but we do know that when you look at who is best
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们确实知道的是，当我们观察——这不完全是无聊，但我们确实知道，当你观察谁最

sentences.en: able to daydream or enjoy their own thoughts, there is a very, very, very, very small, but significant correlation between the amount of time people spend on their cell phones, um,
sentences.zh: 能够白日梦或者享受自己的思绪时，人们花在手机上的时间与

sentences.en: and the extent to which they get bored when trying to daydream that the more time you spend on your
sentences.zh: 他们试图白日梦时感到无聊的程度之间，存在着一个非常、非常、非常、非常小但很显著的相关性，也就是说你在手机上花的时间越多，

sentences.en: phones, uh, you're probably a little bit more likely to be someone that has difficulty, um,
sentences.zh: 呃，你可能就会稍微更有可能成为那种在

sentences.en: enjoying your own thoughts and not getting bored by them.
sentences.zh: 享受自己思绪且不为此感到无聊方面遇到困难的人。

sentences.en: Again, is that causal?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是因果关系吗？

sentences.en: Is it that the cell phone is causing people to have a hard time finding their own thoughts interesting?
sentences.zh: 是因为手机导致人们很难发现自己的思绪有趣吗？

sentences.en: Or is it that people that are sort of prone to boredom are more likely to pick up their phone?
sentences.zh: 还是说那些容易感到无聊的人更有可能拿起手机？

sentences.en: Um, that's really tricky.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的很棘手。

sentences.en: There was a study, this isn't boredom exactly, but there was a study recently
sentences.zh: 曾有一项研究——这不完全是关于无聊的，但最近有这样一项研究

sentences.en: that paid people to not go on social media for a couple of weeks.
sentences.zh: 付钱给人们，让他们在几周内不使用社交媒体。

sentences.en: And they did find that it increased people's happiness and wellbeing when you sort of paid them to stay off for a while.
sentences.zh: 他们确实发现，当你花钱让人们一段时间不上网时，这确实提高了人们的幸福感和福祉。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Oh my God, I guess I'm doomed to be unhappy.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我猜我注定要不快乐了。

sentences.en: Well, another question that occurs to me is whether there's any kind of a link between say overall intelligence and boredom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我脑海中浮现的另一个问题是，总体智力与无聊之间是否存在某种联系。

sentences.en: Like are, are smarter people more likely to not be bored because they've got greater intellectual resources or am I just prejudiced in favor of smart people here?
sentences.zh: 比如，更聪明的人是不是更不容易感到无聊，因为他们拥有更强大的智力资源？还是说我在这里对聪明人有偏见？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's a blessing and a curse because you can get bored for two reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是一把双刃剑，既是福也是祸，因为你可能会出于两个原因感到无聊。

sentences.en: One is you can get bored when something is too hard.
sentences.zh: 一个是当某事太难时，你可能会感到无聊。

sentences.en: And certainly, uh, having sort of more cognitive resources to bring to the table is going to reduce the times when something is too hard for you.
sentences.zh: 当然，呃，拥有更多可资利用的认知资源将会减少某事对你来说太难的情况。

sentences.en: Uh, you simply sort of have a higher baseline chance of finding it interesting.
sentences.zh: 呃，你只是拥有更高的基线几率觉得它有趣。

sentences.en: Um, but boredom is also caused by things that are too easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但无聊也是由太简单的事情引起的。

sentences.en: And so there's actually research.
sentences.zh: 所以其实有这样的研究。

sentences.en: I'm so sorry to tell you that there's actually researched some research that suggests that people with higher IQ or higher need for
sentences.zh: 我很遗憾地告诉你，确实有研究——有一些研究表明，智商更高或认知需求更高的人

sentences.en: cognition may be sort of more susceptible to boredom, especially when it's caused by like
sentences.zh: 可能对无聊更敏感，特别是当无聊是由诸如

sentences.en: repetitive monotonous tasks, precisely because they have so many resources that if you're like,
sentences.zh: 重复单调的任务引起时，正是因为他们拥有如此多的资源，如果你坐在那里，呃，

sentences.en: you're sitting there and, um, you have like say 10 resources and this monotonous boring thing is only occupying two of them.
sentences.zh: 比如你有10种资源，而这个单调无聊的事情只占用了其中的两种。

sentences.en: There's this huge gap between what you are doing and what you could be doing.
sentences.zh: 你在做的事情和你能做的事情之间存在着巨大的鸿沟。

sentences.en: And when that happens, we find it hard to pay attention and that causes boredom.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，我们会发现很难集中注意力，从而导致无聊。

sentences.en: So it's, it's sort of a mixed bag that like, yeah, there may be some instances where more
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像个混合体，比如说，是的，在某些情况下，更

sentences.en: intelligent people have a leg up on finding challenging sort of cognitively demanding tasks, interesting rather than boring.
sentences.zh: 聪明的人在发现具有挑战性的、对认知要求高的任务有趣而不是无聊方面，确实有优势。

sentences.en: We know work from Paul Sylvia suggests that to feel interest in something, there has to be sort of a gap, uh, there where you don't understand it yet,
sentences.zh: 我们知道保罗·西尔维亚（Paul Sylvia）的研究表明，要对某事感到兴趣，其中必须存在某种差距，呃，在那里你还不理解它，

sentences.en: but you feel like you can understand it and intelligence helps with that.
sentences.zh: 但你觉得自己能够理解它，而智力对此有所帮助。

sentences.en: Um, but it also makes you more prone to this other source of boredom.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它也让你更容易受到另一种无聊之源的影响。

sentences.en: And so I think it's, you win some, you lose some, um, in theory, you would think that people who, um, sort of how are smarter would
sentences.zh: 所以我想这是有得有失的，嗯，按理说，你会认为那些更聪明的人

sentences.en: be better at coming up with ways to fix boredom once it comes up.
sentences.zh: 在无聊出现时会更擅长想出办法来解决它。

sentences.en: But what we don't see are strong ties between, uh, emotion regulation, as we call it, when it comes to boredom and intelligence,
sentences.zh: 但我们没有看到我们所说的情绪调节（当涉及到无聊时）与智力之间存在强烈的联系，

sentences.en: it doesn't seem like the case, for instance, necessarily from the very limited evidence that
sentences.zh: 从我们拥有的非常有限的证据来看，似乎情况并不一定是

sentences.en: we have that once you are bored, that your sort of cognitive resources kind of intelligence is going to influence whether or not you're good at escaping that.
sentences.zh: 一旦你感到无聊，你的认知资源即智力就会影响你是否擅长摆脱这种状态。

sentences.en: As you look at the question of boredom, do you all, are you also looking at what makes an individual boring?
sentences.zh: 当你们研究无聊这个问题时，你们是否也在研究是什么让一个人变得无聊？

sentences.en: Is that something that you have examined?
sentences.zh: 这是你们审视过的问题吗？

sentences.en: Can we treat people who are boring?
sentences.zh: 我们可以治疗感到无聊的人吗？

sentences.en: Yes, we, we, we have, um, this is very, none of this is published yet.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们，我们，我们有，嗯，这些都还没有发表。

sentences.en: It's still very exploratory.
sentences.zh: 它仍然非常具探索性。

sentences.en: There's some work that Karen Gasper and colleagues are doing on this question that suggests, um, that when someone bores us in conversation, we, we think badly of them.
sentences.zh: 卡伦·加斯珀（Karen Gasper）及其同事正在就这个问题开展一些研究，这表明，嗯，当我们在对话中让人感到厌烦时，我们会对他们产生不好的看法。

sentences.en: Uh, there's also work that
sentences.zh: 呃，还有一些研究

sentences.en: I've been doing on what I call the only boring people are boring, uh, or only boring people get bored.
sentences.zh: 是我一直在做的，关于我所谓的“只有无聊的人才会无聊”，呃，或者“只有无聊的人才会感到无聊”。

sentences.en: I thought, which is right.
sentences.zh: 我以为，这是对的。

sentences.en: This idea that if you're bored, there must be something wrong with you.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，如果你感到无聊，你身上一定有什么地方出了问题。

sentences.en: And the thing that's wrong with you is probably that you're a boring person.
sentences.zh: 而你身上出问题的地方可能就是你是一个无聊的人。

sentences.en: And so I've been looking at people's stereotypes about what is a boring person like, um, what do you think about boring people?
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在研究人们对无聊的人是什么样的刻板印象，嗯，你对无聊的人有什么看法？

sentences.en: Are people responsible for their own boredom?
sentences.zh: 人们要为自己的无聊负责吗？

sentences.en: And all of that work is very preliminary.
sentences.zh: 所有这些研究都还非常初步。

sentences.en: So we don't have good answers right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在还没有好的答案。

sentences.en: Um, but what I can tell you so far is that what you sort of lay guesses or an intuition look like are pretty consistent with what we're seeing in how people
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我目前能告诉你的是，你们的日常猜测或直觉与我们在人们如何

sentences.en: are rating boring people and who seems boring to them.
sentences.zh: 评价无聊的人以及谁对他们来说显得无聊方面所看到的情况相当一致。

sentences.en: Um, there is work and I love this work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一项研究——我非常喜欢这项研究。

sentences.en: So
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: I'm just going to drop it in here that if you're worried about being boring, the chances are, um, that you're not as boring as you think you are.
sentences.zh: 我只想顺便提一下，如果你担心自己很无聊，那么发生的几率是，嗯，你并没有自己想象的那么无聊。

sentences.en: Uh, there's great work by, um, Peggy Clark and, um,
sentences.zh: 呃，佩吉·克拉克（Peggy Clark）和

sentences.en: and colleagues that show that there's this sort of liking gap that we all kind of think that we're like less interesting and more boring and less likable than we actually are.
sentences.zh: 同事们做了一项很棒的研究，表明存在着这样一种“喜爱鸿沟”（liking gap），我们都倾向于认为自己比实际情况更不有趣、更无聊、更不受欢迎。

sentences.en: But if you actually put us in conversations with each other and ask your partner, how you were, they tend to sort of rate you more positively.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的让我们互相交谈，并问你的伴侣你表现如何，他们往往会给你更积极的评价。

sentences.en: So when it comes to worrying about you being boring, you're probably not as boring as you think you are.
sentences.zh: 所以当谈到担心自己很无聊时，你可能并没有自己想象的那么无聊。

sentences.en: That's good to hear, especially for people who are kind of locked up with the same people day after day right now.
sentences.zh: 很高兴听到这个，特别是对现在日复一日和同一群人关在一起的人来说。

sentences.en: You know, I was also looking at the work that you've been doing around categorization, which I found interesting because I'm a birder.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我还在看你围绕分类所做的研究，我觉得这很有趣，因为我是一个观鸟者。

sentences.en: So when I'm not stuck in the house, I mean, I like to go out and look at birds and some people think that that's crazy,
sentences.zh: 所以当我没有被困在家时，我是说，我喜欢出去看鸟，有些人觉得这很疯狂，

sentences.en: but why are collecting and categorizing, um, interesting to some of us and, and some of us find it inherently meaningful?
sentences.zh: 但为什么收集和分类，嗯，对我们中的一些人来说很有趣，而且我们中的一些人发现它本质上有意义？

sentences.en: Uh, I love that you asked this.
sentences.zh: 呃，我很高兴你问了这个。

sentences.en: I have a question for you.
sentences.zh: 我有个问题想问你。

sentences.en: Do you have a favorite bird?
sentences.zh: 你有最喜欢的鸟吗？

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: That's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难说。

sentences.en: Where I live, one of the birds that I love to see, particularly this time of year, the male wood ducks, I think they're so beautiful, but I mean, there are so many,
sentences.zh: 在我住的地方，我喜欢看到的鸟之一，特别是每年的这个时候，雄性林鸳鸯，我觉得它们太美了，但我的意思是，有那么多

sentences.en: resplendent cats all, I mean, how could, you know, but roseate spoonbill, I could go on and on with birds.
sentences.zh: 华丽的……我的意思是，怎么能……你知道的，还有粉红琵鹭，关于鸟类我可以说个没完。

sentences.en: You see, now I'm going to get boring.
sentences.zh: 你看，现在我要变得无聊了。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Um, so the roseate spoonbills just came to
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以粉红琵鹭刚刚来到

sentences.en: Florida.
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: So I've been very, I went out to see them right before all the lockdown stuff happened.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直非常……就在所有封城的事情发生之前，我特意出去看它们。

sentences.en: That was very exciting.
sentences.zh: 那太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: Um, and I ask you because I think people who are into birds, you can hear it, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我问你是因为我觉得喜欢鸟的人，你能听出来，对吧？

sentences.en: It's exciting.
sentences.zh: 这很令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And, uh, I have gotten into birding as a result of this research interest, um, because I was looking at categorization and I was really struck by how many people I, when I talk
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，由于这个研究兴趣，我也迷上了观鸟，嗯，因为我在研究分类，而且我真的对当我谈论这个时有多少人感到震惊

sentences.en: about this in lectures, I'm always, I always ask the audience, does anyone here, is anyone here a bird watcher or a birder?
sentences.zh: 在讲座中，我总是，我总是问观众，这里有人吗，这里有人是观鸟者吗？

sentences.en: And, uh, inevitably one or two people kind of raise their hands often kind of shy.
sentences.zh: 然后，不可避免地会有一两个人举手，通常都带点害羞。

sentences.en: We get a bad rap.
sentences.zh: 我们名声不太好。

sentences.en: No, I mean, and then I make it worse.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，然后我让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: I'm like, isn't it hilarious that grown adults go out and like count things like in the world, but it is in the most wonderful of ways.
sentences.zh: 我会说，成年人出去数世界上的东西，这难道不搞笑吗，但这却以最美妙的方式呈现出来。

sentences.en: Like I think it's absolutely wonderful.
sentences.zh: 就像我认为这绝对美妙一样。

sentences.en: And I think what's happening here is we've done a number of studies.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这里发生的事情是，我们做过许多研究。

sentences.en: We're writing this up for publication right now that what categorization does for us and by categorization, I mean, any of these categorization hobbies.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正在把这些写成文章准备发表：分类为我们做了什么——通过分类，我的意思是任何这些分类爱好。

sentences.en: So shell collecting bird watching, um, this work was actually inspired by a scuba diving trip, uh, to Honduras where I brought
sentences.zh: 所以贝壳收集、观鸟，嗯，这项研究其实是由一次去洪都拉斯的深潜之旅启发而来的，当时我带了

sentences.en: a fish identification chart with me on the boat and everyone was making fun of me until we got in
sentences.zh: 一张鱼类识别图上船，每个人都在取笑我，直到我们下水

sentences.en: the water and then they all wanted my identification chart and I didn't have it anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后他们都想要我的识别图，而我没有了。

sentences.en: And I was like, well, you'd want to know this information.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，嗯，你们会想知道这些信息的。

sentences.en: And, um, we think what's happening is that when you see something, especially something that doesn't, you don't have a good conception of, or that doesn't
sentences.zh: 而且，嗯，我们认为发生的情况是，当你看到某样东西时，特别是某种你没有很好的概念、或者

sentences.en: make sense to you or you haven't made sense of, uh, categorization is a way of helping you
sentences.zh: 对你来说说不通、或者你还没弄明白的东西，分类是一种帮助你

sentences.en: literally create order and coherence in the world that imagine, for instance, you're not a birder and
sentences.zh: 字面意思上在世界上建立秩序和连贯性的方法。试想一下，例如，你不是一个观鸟者，

sentences.en: you just heard our conversation about all these birds and you're just like, oh my God, there's just all these birds.
sentences.zh: 你刚刚听了我们关于所有这些鸟类的对话，你就会想，哦天哪，这里有这么多的鸟。

sentences.en: What categorization lets you do is break that down into like, oh no, there's this kind of bird and there's this kind of bird and there's this kind of bird.
sentences.zh: 分类能让你做的是把它分解开来，比如，哦不，有这种鸟，有那种鸟，还有这种鸟。

sentences.en: And we know that when we see patterns in the world, they feel meaningful to us.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，当我们看到世界上的模式时，它们对我们来说是有意义的。

sentences.en: That patterns give us a sense of meaning, whether it's being able to sort of recognize and see patterns in the wildflowers or the birds, or just even our own daily routines.
sentences.zh: 模式给我们一种意义感，无论是能够识别和看到野花或鸟类中的模式，还是仅仅是我们自己的日常琐事。

sentences.en: Uh, Samantha Heinzelman has wonderful work that shows that people who have more routine in their lives experience more meaning in life.
sentences.zh: 萨曼莎·海因泽尔曼（Samantha Heinzelman）有很棒的研究表明，生活中常规更多的人在生活中体验到更多的意义。

sentences.en: And they also feel like their lives are more meaningful while they're engaged in those routines.
sentences.zh: 当他们在进行这些常规活动时，他们也觉得自己的生活更有意义。

sentences.en: We really value this kind of predictability and coherence.
sentences.zh: 我们非常珍视这种可预测性和连贯性。

sentences.en: And that's what categorization gives us is when we look at this big sort of mess out there
sentences.zh: 这就是分类给我们的东西：当我们看着外面这个巨大的乱七八糟的

sentences.en: in the world, and then we can order it and put it into little boxes that lets us make sense of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 世界，然后我们能够将其整理并放进小盒子时，这能让我们理解正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: And we experienced that sense of making sense of what's happening as a sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 我们将这种理解正在发生的事情的体验视为一种意义感。

sentences.en: And that's a really powerful feeling for most of us.
sentences.zh: 这对我们大多数人来说是一种非常强大的感觉。

sentences.en: And it also, because meaning is related to boredom, it reduces boredom and increases interest and enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 而且，由于意义与无聊有关，它能减少无聊，并增加兴趣和享受。

sentences.en: I think that's great.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很棒。

sentences.en: I mean, it reminds me of taking walks in the woods with somebody who can identify plants, how that's a different experience from just walking and looking and not knowing what
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这让我想起和能够辨认植物的人一起在树林里散步，这与只是散步、观看却不知道你看到的是什么

sentences.en: you're seeing.
sentences.zh: 有着完全不同的体验。

sentences.en: Just taking a tour of an art museum and having a docent or getting the headphones so that you understand what you're looking at.
sentences.zh: 就像参观艺术博物馆时有导游讲解，或者戴上耳机以便你理解你看到的东西一样。

sentences.en: It certainly makes a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 这绝对说得通。

sentences.en: No, it's a completely different experience.
sentences.zh: 不，这完全是不同的体验。

sentences.en: You know, in social psychology, we talk a lot about construals, and that your emotions and behavior and thoughts are shaped on your construal or sort of
sentences.zh: 你知道，在社会心理学中，我们经常谈论建构（construals），你的情绪、行为和思想都是基于你的建构或对你所见事物的理解而塑造的。

sentences.en: understanding of what you're seeing.
sentences.zh: 而分类改变了这一点。

sentences.en: And categorization changes that.
sentences.zh: 而分类改变了这一点。

sentences.en: When you see this painting as when you understand its full historical significance, or you understand that that weird little ugly plant
sentences.zh: 当你看到这幅画，就像你理解了它全部的历史意义，或者你明白那个奇怪的小丑植物

sentences.en: there is actually a really rare and valuable native species that eats ants or something insane.
sentences.zh: 其实是一个非常罕见且珍贵的本地物种，会吃蚂蚁之类的疯狂东西。

sentences.en: It's a fundamentally different experience on every single level.
sentences.zh: 这在各个层面上都是一种根本不同的体验。

sentences.en: You've also done research into procrastination, which I have to say, it kind of seems like you're
sentences.zh: 你还对拖延症做过研究，我不得不说，这看起来好像你是在

sentences.en: trying to put a positive spin on a lot of stuff we do that gets a bad rap for being unimportant and not socially useful.
sentences.zh: 试图为我们做的很多被冠以不重要、对社会无用等恶名的事情进行正面粉饰。

sentences.en: But what are you learning about procrastination and that grow out of your your work on boredom?
sentences.zh: 但是，关于拖延症，你从对无聊的研究中获得了什么启发，又学到了什么？

sentences.en: So procrastination, there's a saying in psychology, right, that research is research.
sentences.zh: 所以关于拖延症，心理学上有一句名言，对吧，研究就是研究。

sentences.en: I started working on procrastination as an undergraduate in a course that I took on motivation and self-regulation,
sentences.zh: 我作为一名本科生时，在一门关于动机与自我调节的课程中开始研究拖延症，

sentences.en: because I wanted to understand why I procrastinated all the time.
sentences.zh: 因为我想搞懂自己为什么总是拖延。

sentences.en: And what I found out was really interesting is I went to a really small liberal arts college, where there was this really strong
sentences.zh: 而我发现一件非常有趣的事，我当时在一所很小的文理学院，那里有着非常强烈的

sentences.en: sort of sense of academic identity, and people really valued, you know, this idea of the intellectual life and academia for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 某种学术认同感，人们真的很看重，你知道的，这种知识分子生活和学术本身就是目的的理念。

sentences.en: And so it manifested in a lot of, like, academic bragging, but like, not like I got a good grade, but like, I stayed up until 6am working on my paper, like,
sentences.zh: 所以这体现在很多类似学术吹牛的现象上，但不是说我得了好成绩，而是像我熬夜到早上六点写论文，就像

sentences.en: and someone else was like, Oh, yeah, I haven't left the library in 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 另一个人会说，哦，对啊，我已经48小时没离开过图书馆了。

sentences.en: My college actually started closing the library at 2am to prevent this kind of like, insane behavior.
sentences.zh: 我的大学实际上开始在凌晨2点关闭图书馆，以防止这种类似疯狂的行为。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I became really interested in this question, because what I noticed was that many of my peers that would brag
sentences.zh: 我开始对这个问题非常感兴趣，因为我注意到，我的许多同龄人会吹嘘

sentences.en: about like, having done nothing but work on this paper for the past week, would be failing half their classes.
sentences.zh: 过去一周除了写这篇论文什么都没做，结果却挂了他们一半的课。

sentences.en: And I was like, Well, is it possible that you can procrastinate in ways that aren't what we typically conceptualize procrastination as?
sentences.zh: 当时我在想，有没有可能你拖延的方式，并不是我们通常所概念化理解的拖延呢？

sentences.en: So we often think of procrastination, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常认为的拖延，对吧？

sentences.en: Is that instead of doing the thing you're supposed to be doing, you go off and watch Netflix, or you go to
sentences.zh: 就是不去干你该干的事，而是跑去刷网飞，或者去

sentences.en: a party, or you know, you do something that's sort of like fun and trivial.
sentences.zh: 参加派对，又或者你知道的，去做一些既有趣又琐碎的事。

sentences.en: But that wasn't what I saw the students doing at this college, what I saw them doing was procrastinating on things that they really should have been doing.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是我在那所大学里看到的学生们的做法，我看到的是他们在拖延那些他们真正该做的事。

sentences.en: But they were procrastinating by doing other important things, they were doing other important schoolwork as a way of avoiding this, this task that they were putting
sentences.zh: 但他们拖延的方式是去做其他重要的事情，他们在做其他重要的功课，以此来逃避这个他们由于某种原因

sentences.en: off for some reason.
sentences.zh: 一直在推迟的任务。

sentences.en: And so I became interested in what I call productive procrastination.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始对所谓的“生产性拖延”感兴趣。

sentences.en: And by that, I mean, procrastinating on something by doing something else that still has value.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通过做另一件同样有价值的事情来拖延某件事。

sentences.en: So like I said, studying for an exam, instead of watching Netflix, or it doesn't have to be in the same domain,
sentences.zh: 所以就像我说的，复习考试而不是看网飞，或者它不一定在同一个领域，

sentences.en: you can procrastinate on one academic task, or working on another academic task, and that could be productive.
sentences.zh: 你可以拖延一个学术任务，转而去处理另一个学术任务，这也可以是富有成效的。

sentences.en: But you can also procrastinate on that academic task by doing the laundry or washing the dishes or baking bread or doing something that's productive, but not necessarily academic.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以通过洗衣服、洗碗、烤面包或做一些虽然有成效但不一定是学术的事情来拖延那个学术任务。

sentences.en: And so I got really interested in this question of like, one, is this a real thing?
sentences.zh: 所以我对这个问题产生了浓厚的兴趣：第一，这真的是个真实存在的现象吗？

sentences.en: Or am I just sort of like, making this up?
sentences.zh: 还是我只是凭空捏造出来的？

sentences.en: Like, do people actually engage in these different kinds of procrastination?
sentences.zh: 比如说，人们真的会进行这些不同种类的拖延吗？

sentences.en: And two, if they do, is, is it as bad as these classic ways of procrastinating, like blowing off your work to go party with friends or watch TV?
sentences.zh: 第二，如果他们真的这样做，它像那些传统的拖延方式那样糟糕吗，比如旷掉工作去和朋友开派对或看电视？

sentences.en: And what we found was like twofold.
sentences.zh: 而我们发现的结果是双重的。

sentences.en: So first of all, people absolutely report doing this.
sentences.zh: 首先，人们确实报告说他们会这样做。

sentences.en: And this idea is out there everywhere in pop culture.
sentences.zh: 这种想法在流行文化中随处可见。

sentences.en: Procrastibaking, right, is totally a phrase that people use.
sentences.zh: 比如“拖延烘焙”（procrastibaking），这绝对是人们常用的一个词。

sentences.en: It was in the New York Times not too long ago.
sentences.zh: 不久前它还出现在《纽约时报》上。

sentences.en: It's like a guide to procrastibaking.
sentences.zh: 就像是一份“拖延烘焙指南”。

sentences.en: And we see people talk about it in everyday life, but we don't see it showing up in their research.
sentences.zh: 我们看到人们在日常生活中谈论它，但我们没有看到它出现在他们的研究中。

sentences.en: So we just designed a study asking people, very descriptive, qualitative-ish study, basically looking at whether people first just do this.
sentences.zh: 所以我们专门设计了一项研究来询问人们，这是一项非常具描述性的、偏定性的研究，主要考察人们是否首先会这样做。

sentences.en: And they do.
sentences.zh: 他们确实会。

sentences.en: It is as common, if not more common than these sort of old school traditional ideas of
sentences.zh: 这与那些老派传统的拖延观念一样普遍，甚至更普遍，

sentences.en: procrastination, where you put off one important task by doing something unimportant or a blow off thing instead.
sentences.zh: 即通过做一些不重要的事情或逃避现实的事情来推迟一项重要任务。

sentences.en: People were just as likely to say that they are putting off academic tasks by doing work for other classes or putting off a hard assignment by doing an easier assignment or
sentences.zh: 人们同样很可能会说，他们通过为其他课程做作业来推迟学术任务，或者通过做更简单的作业来推迟困难的作业，或者

sentences.en: putting off school work by cleaning the dishes.
sentences.zh: 通过洗碗来推迟学校的功课。

sentences.en: That was just as common as these kinds, as watching
sentences.zh: 这和看网飞或者

sentences.en: Netflix or, you know, doing something that had no point.
sentences.zh: 做一些毫无意义的事情一样普遍。

sentences.en: And it's not just college students.
sentences.zh: 而且不只是大学生。

sentences.en: Most of the work that we've done has been in academia and academics, both for convenience and because that's where it's an obvious issue.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的大部分工作都是在学术界和学者群体中展开的，既为了便利，也是因为那是一个显而易见的问题所在。

sentences.en: But we've also done some work, for instance, with visitors to the
sentences.zh: 但我们也做了一些研究，例如针对

sentences.en: North Carolina State Fair, which is a much broader group of people.
sentences.zh: 北卡罗来纳州集市（North Carolina State Fair）游客的研究，那是一个更广泛的人群。

sentences.en: It's just people that went to the fair and agreed to participate in a psych study.
sentences.zh: 他们只是去了集市并同意参与心理学研究的人。

sentences.en: And we see similar rates when you ask about procrastinating on tasks at work or procrastinating on tasks around the home.
sentences.zh: 当我们询问有关工作中的任务拖延或家务任务拖延时，我们看到了类似的比率。

sentences.en: So for instance, I have still not filed my IRS returns.
sentences.zh: 比如，我到现在还没报税。

sentences.en: I'm absolutely procrastinating on that.
sentences.zh: 我绝对是在拖延这件事。

sentences.en: But I feel justified because I've been working on grant applications.
sentences.zh: 但我感到理直气壮，因为我一直在忙着写经费申请。

sentences.en: Well, and they changed the deadline this year, too.
sentences.zh: 而且今年他们还更改了截止日期。

sentences.en: Oh, no, they changed the deadline.
sentences.zh: 哦不，他们改了截止日期。

sentences.en: I will pretend like that's the reason why.
sentences.zh: 我要假装这就是原因所在。

sentences.en: But it also sounds like an issue of prioritization.
sentences.zh: 但这也听起来像是一个优先级排序的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I certainly work with people who, if you don't tell them, look, this is the most important thing you need to do today,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实共事过这样的人，如果你不告诉他们，听着，这是你今天必须做的最重要的事情，

sentences.en: that they don't understand that they'll do the thing that's maybe fifth or sixth down the list in my mind.
sentences.zh: 他们就不会明白，他们会去做在我看来可能排在第五或第六位的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, is that different or is that the same kind of procrastination?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这与那种拖延不同还是相同的？

sentences.en: Um, I think it's subjective.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为这是主观的。

sentences.en: I think it counts as procrastination when you know you should be doing it, but choose not to.
sentences.zh: 我认为当你明知应该去做却选择不做时，这就构成了拖延。

sentences.en: So if you legitimately don't think you should be doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你真心认为自己不该做那件事。

sentences.en: So I think that's actually why this is a great example.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这其实就是为什么这是一个极好的例子。

sentences.en: I think the tax return is procrastination in my case, because I am, I know I should be doing it.
sentences.zh: 我认为对我来说报税就是拖延，因为我在，我知道我应该去做。

sentences.en: And I'm deliberately putting it off by doing other things that make me feel better about it.
sentences.zh: 而我却故意通过做其他能让我感觉好一点的事情来推迟它。

sentences.en: I'm doing it.
sentences.zh: 我在做那些事。

sentences.en: But someone else, like my father also hasn't filed his tax return, isn't planning to do so until the end of April.
sentences.zh: 但其他人，比如我父亲也还没报税，他不打算在四月底之前做这件事。

sentences.en: But in his case, he rationally looked at the extended deadline and said, um, you know what, like, it makes sense for
sentences.zh: 但在他的情况下，他理性地看了看延长的截止日期，然后说，嗯，你知道吗，

sentences.en: me to wait and do this later because there's this other really important stuff I have to do.
sentences.zh: 我等会儿再做是合乎情理的，因为我还有其他非常重要的事要做。

sentences.en: And in that case, I would say that is not procrastinating.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，我会说这不是拖延。

sentences.en: He does, he's not putting it off.
sentences.zh: 他没有在推迟。

sentences.en: He doesn't think he should do it now.
sentences.zh: 他不认为自己现在就该去做。

sentences.en: Uh, he very legitimately has simply reordered his priorities to reflect.
sentences.zh: 呃，他非常合乎逻辑地重新排列了自己的优先级来反映这一点。

sentences.en: So it's a conscious decision.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个有意识的决定。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so I think procrastination is in some ways a subjective state that it, it depends on the psychology of why people are doing it and how they feel about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得拖延在某种程度上是一种主观状态，它取决于人们为什么要这样做以及他们对此有何感受的心理学。

sentences.en: Uh, the good news, um, this is very preliminary, but we do have data that for academic procrastination,
sentences.zh: 好消息是，呃，这还非常初步，但我们确实有关于学术拖延的数据，

sentences.en: at least that, um, I'm not going to go so far as to say you should do productive procrastination.
sentences.zh: 至少，呃，我不会走得太远去宣称你应该去做生产性拖延。

sentences.en: That's definitely too far.
sentences.zh: 那绝对有点过头了。

sentences.en: But when we compare people that don't procrastinate at all, which is an embarrassingly large percentage of humanity I've discovered.
sentences.zh: 但是当我们把那些根本不拖延的人进行对比时，我发现这是一个令人尴尬的巨大比例的人类。

sentences.en: Um, I know depending on the study, it's, you know, you have like 25 to 30, 40% of people that like, you know, they, everyone's
sentences.zh: 呃，我知道根据不同的研究，大概有25%到30%、40%的人，你知道的，每个人都是

sentences.en: human, but by and large, they tend not to procrastinate.
sentences.zh: 人，但大体上，他们倾向于不拖延。

sentences.en: Um, when you look at people that engage in a lot of productive procrastination, so putting off their taxes to apply for grants,
sentences.zh: 呃，当你看看那些从事大量生产性拖延的人，比如推迟报税去申请经费，

sentences.en: are putting off, uh, studying for an exam to work on a paper assignment, they don't look any different in terms of their college GPAs.
sentences.zh: 或者推迟复习考试去写论文作业，他们在大学平均绩点（GPA）上并没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Uh, their GPAs look about the same.
sentences.zh: 呃，他们的GPA看起来差不多。

sentences.en: It doesn't look like their grades are suffering because of this, uh, decision overall.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，他们的成绩似乎并没有因为这个呃决定而受到影响。

sentences.en: Uh, the other thing that we find is that when you engage in productive procrastination in this way, it doesn't seem like
sentences.zh: 呃，我们发现的另一件事是，当你以这种方式进行生产性拖延时，它似乎

sentences.en: it puts you at risk for alcohol use and risky alcohol drinking, uh, in the same way that we often see with other forms of procrastination.
sentences.zh: 不会像我们在其他形式的拖延中经常看到的那样，让你面临酗酒和危险饮酒的风险。

sentences.en: So that classic procrastination where you blow off your schoolwork to go party or go, um, watch Netflix that's associated with a lot of problems,
sentences.zh: 所以那种经典的拖延，即你旷掉功课去开派对或者去呃看网飞，与很多问题息息相关，

sentences.en: just with self-regulation in general and self-control in general.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是与整体的自我调节和整体的自我控制有关。

sentences.en: And we see a lot of correlations there between people that procrastinate in those ways and increased risk of alcohol use disorder, increased
sentences.zh: 我们在那些以这种方式拖延的人与增加的酒精使用障碍风险、增加的

sentences.en: risk of hazardous drinking in college, uh, you know, binge drinking, all that sort of stuff tends to go along as a package with that behavioral profile.
sentences.zh: 大学危险饮酒风险、呃，你知道的，痛饮狂欢，所有这些事情之间看到了很多相关性，它们往往作为该行为特征的整体打包出现。

sentences.en: And that's really not what we see for the productive procrastinators.
sentences.zh: 而这真的不是我们在生产性拖延者身上看到的。

sentences.en: Um, I'm writing up a paper right now, but our current thinking is that productive procrastination may be an unorthodox, but acceptable variant that people
sentences.zh: 呃，我目前正在写一篇论文，但我们目前的想法是，生产性拖延可能是一种非正统但可接受的变体，人们

sentences.en: use to emotionally cope with tasks that are difficult and hard for them to do in some way that at least you're not totally disengaging.
sentences.zh: 用它来在情感上应对那些对他们来说在某种程度上困难且难以完成的任务，至少你没有完全抽离。

sentences.en: You know, if I'm having a really hard time on this school assignment and I decided to work on this other assignment for school, I'm still engaged academically.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果我在这个学校作业上遇到很大困难，而我决定去做另一个学校作业，我仍然在学术上保持投入。

sentences.en: I'm not losing my overall academic motivation.
sentences.zh: 我没有失去整体的学术动力。

sentences.en: Uh, and I may be better prepared to circle back and work on that original task that I put off at a later date.
sentences.zh: 呃，我可能做好了更好的准备，能够在晚些时候回过头来处理我推迟的那个原始任务。

sentences.en: So productive procrastination, I wouldn't go so far as to say that a positive or a good thing, but I don't think it's a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 所以生产性拖延，我不会走得太远去说它是一件积极的或好的事情，但我不认为这是一件坏事。

sentences.en: And I don't think people need to feel as guilty about that kind of procrastination as they do for, you know, just blowing it all off and going and doing something fun instead.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为人们不需要对那种拖延感到像那种仅仅把事情全抛在一边、跑去玩乐所感受到的那样内疚。

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 对，这说得通。

sentences.en: Any final words of advice for our listeners who might be feeling bored or maybe putting off doing things that they could be doing right now?
sentences.zh: 对于那些可能感到无聊或者一直在推迟他们现在就能做的事情的听众，你有什么最后的建议吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: So I, I have, I'm going to tackle those separately because I have, I have two sets of tips.
sentences.zh: 所以，我，我打算分开来谈，因为我有，我有两套建议。

sentences.en: One for procrastination, Alexandra Forenden-Zurek has fabulous data showing that there's a really nifty trick that you can do with procrastination to help.
sentences.zh: 关于拖延，亚历山大·弗伦登-祖雷克（Alexandra Froenden-Zurek）有极棒的数据表明，你可以对拖延使用一个非常巧妙的诀窍来提供帮助。

sentences.en: And I read about this in the research literature.
sentences.zh: 我在研究文献中读到过这个。

sentences.en: I cite it in my papers all the time and I use it in my own life and I've personally replicated it with a sample of one many times.
sentences.zh: 我一直在我的论文中引用它，我在自己的生活中使用它，并且我曾多次在只有我一个人的样本上亲自复制了它。

sentences.en: Uh, and I find it helpful.
sentences.zh: 呃，我发现它很有用。

sentences.en: Uh, and the idea is that a lot of times when you're dreading doing a task, there's two different reasons you might dread doing it.
sentences.zh: 这个想法是，很多时候当你害怕做一项任务时，你可能会害怕做它有两个不同的原因。

sentences.en: You might dread actually doing it.
sentences.zh: 你可能害怕真的去做它。

sentences.en: Like, Oh, I don't want to sit down and do this super monotonous, complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我不想坐下来做这个超级单调、复杂的事情。

sentences.en: Or you might dread doing it because the stakes are so high.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会害怕做它，因为利害关系太高了。

sentences.en: Like, Oh, I know it's just this one little email to send to someone, but I'm really worried about how they're going to respond.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我知道这只是给某人发的一封小小邮件，但我真的很担心他们会如何回应。

sentences.en: And if they respond badly, it's going to ruin everything.
sentences.zh: 如果他们回应得很糟糕，那就全完了。

sentences.en: And so what Alexandra Forenden finds is that if you can figure out why you're putting it off, uh, you can focus on the other thing instead.
sentences.zh: 所以亚历山大·弗伦登发现的是，如果你能弄清楚你为什么在推迟它，呃，你就可以把注意力集中在另一件事情上。

sentences.en: So if you don't want to do your taxes, because I don't want to go and find all the little forms and do all the little numbers and like, where's my W2?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你不想报税，因为我不想去寻找所有的小表格，处理所有的小数字，比如我的W-2表格在哪里？

sentences.en: Oh, I moved institutions.
sentences.zh: 哦，我换了机构。

sentences.en: I need to find my lap, you know, all these little, like the nitty gritty details by shifting my focus to why I'm doing it.
sentences.zh: 我需要找到我的实验室，你知道的，所有这些细枝末节，通过将我的注意力转移到我为什么要这样做上。

sentences.en: The bigger overarching abstract goal, like, Oh, uh, you know, I'm going to get a tax refund.
sentences.zh: 那个更大的、包罗万象的抽象目标，比如，哦，呃，你知道的，我会拿到退税。

sentences.en: I'm going to not get in trouble with the IRS that can increase motivation and make it easier to actually just get started and do the task.
sentences.zh: 我不会惹上税务局的麻烦，这可以增加动力，并使人更容易真正开始并完成任务。

sentences.en: So if you're put off by the detail, the nitty gritty details, focusing on the bigger reason for why you're doing it helps.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你被细节、细枝末节所困扰，专注于你为什么要这样做的宏大理由会有所帮助。

sentences.en: And conversely, if you're putting it off, because the big reason that you're doing it
sentences.zh: 反过来，如果你在推迟它，因为你这样做的宏大理由

sentences.en: is so, uh, you know, stressful or, or overwhelming, it helps to instead shift to the nitty gritty
sentences.zh: 是如此地，呃，你知道的，充满压力或令人不知所措，转而关注细枝末节

sentences.en: details and be like, okay, like, you know, instead of focusing about like how this email is going to
sentences.zh: 并心想，好吧，你知道的，与其纠结这封邮件将如何

sentences.en: make or break my career, I'm just going to focus on writing it one word at a time.
sentences.zh: 决定我职业生涯的成败，我不如专注于把它写下来，一次写一个词。

sentences.en: And that kind of shift in level helps people fix the problem.
sentences.zh: 这种层面的转变有助于人们解决问题。

sentences.en: And I think that's actually a valuable lesson for boredom in general, because often, not always, but procrastination is about anticipating that
sentences.zh: 我认为这其实也是应对整体无聊感的一个宝贵经验，因为通常（并非总是），拖延是关于预期

sentences.en: something's going to make you feel anxious or anticipating that something's going to make you feel bored.
sentences.zh: 某事会让你感到焦虑，或者预期某事会让你感到无聊。

sentences.en: And we know that we can reduce boredom by fixing the problems that caused it.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，通过解决导致无聊的问题，我们可以减少无聊感。

sentences.en: You know, so we opened today where it's talking about how boredom signals that you're not able to pay attention or
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们今天开场时谈到过无聊如何表明你无法集中注意力，或者

sentences.en: that what you're doing doesn't feel meaning, but that also gives you the information you need to stop feeling bored.
sentences.zh: 你正在做的事情感觉不到意义，但这也为你提供了停止感到无聊所需的信息。

sentences.en: If you feel bored because what you're doing doesn't have meaning, maybe you should either go do something else, or find a way to see the meaning in what you're doing.
sentences.zh: 如果你因为所做的事情没有意义而感到无聊，也许你该要么去做别的事，要么找到一种方法去发现你正在做的事情的意义。

sentences.en: So for right now, for instance, we're all under these stay at home orders.
sentences.zh: 所以就目前而言，例如，我们都处在这些居家令之下。

sentences.en: And that doesn't feel like we're doing much.
sentences.zh: 这感觉不像我们在做什么大事。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel super meaningful.
sentences.zh: 感觉不是超级有意义。

sentences.en: I know it is objectively, but doesn't feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我知道客观上是这样，但感觉上并非如此。

sentences.en: So anything we can do to remind ourselves and keep that frame in mind that what I'm doing right now, literally by sitting at my desk is saving lives, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以做任何事来提醒自己并保持这种框架：我此刻正在做的事情，仅仅是通过坐在办公桌前，就是在拯救生命，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, any way that you can increase the meaning of what you're doing, whether that's a reminder on the fridge or talking about it with
sentences.zh: 你知道的，任何能增加你所做事情意义的方式，无论是冰箱上的便签还是与

sentences.en: others, it literally makes us feel less bored because it infuses everything you're doing with a sense of meaning.
sentences.zh: 他人交谈，它确实让我们感到不那么无聊，因为它给你的每一项行动都注入了一种意义感。

sentences.en: And that sort of quiets down all those sort of like parts of your mind that are alerting you that what you're doing isn't meaningful because you're saying, yes, yes, it is.
sentences.zh: 这就平息了你大脑中那些警告你你做的事情没有意义的部分，因为你在说：不，不，它很有意义。

sentences.en: And the same thing goes for attention that if you're having trouble concentrating, because things are too hard right now, it's okay to listen to that signal and back off and,
sentences.zh: 注意力也是如此，如果你因为现在事情太难而难以集中注意力，倾听这个信号并退后一步是没问题的，而且，

sentences.en: you know, step it down to a level that you can handle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，把它降到你能应付的水平。

sentences.en: Or conversely, if you don't have enough to occupy your days, sort of use it as license.
sentences.zh: 或者相反，如果你没有足够的事情来填满你的日子，就把这当成一种许可。

sentences.en: If that's where you're at, not everyone is, but if you're at that point where you want to engage in some new hobbies or download that book
sentences.zh: 如果你正处于那种状态（并非所有人都是，但如果你正处于那种想要培养一些新爱好或下载那本

sentences.en: you've always been meeting during, that can be a great fit for people too.
sentences.zh: 你一直想在期间阅读的的书籍的节点），那对人们来说也会是一个极好的契合点。

sentences.en: I think fixing boredom and fixing procrastination are really about listening to your emotions and listening to the information that those emotions are trying to tell you.
sentences.zh: 我认为解决无聊和解决拖延症，实际上是要倾听你的情绪，并倾听这些情绪试图告诉你的一些信息。

sentences.en: We have this idea that emotions are irrational and they're not.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种观念认为情绪是不理性的，但其实它们不是。

sentences.en: They're so rational.
sentences.zh: 它们非常理性。

sentences.en: They're like our internal messaging service to tell us what's going on with our minds.
sentences.zh: 它们就像我们的内部消息服务，告诉我们大脑中正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And by listening to them, we can get that information and use that information to fix them and feel better.
sentences.zh: 通过倾听它们，我们可以获取这些信息并利用这些信息来解决问题，让自己感觉更好。

sentences.en: Well, that's all great advice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些都是很好的建议。

sentences.zh: 韦斯特盖特博士，非常感谢您能参加。
